title: Sleepy Cues: The Right Moment for Sleep
summary:
Your baby sends signals that tell you what they feel and what they need. When they are tired or need a break, they may turn their head away from you, yawn, or start to fuss. Every baby has their own way, so learn your own baby's signals by watching calmly, and respond to them; your response makes them feel safe and loved, and it is fine to hold them and respond to them whenever they need it.

When you notice these signals, help them calm down: lower the lights, lower your voice, and cut down on play and excitement; too much excitement before sleep can wake them up instead of calming them. If they seem sleepy, put them on their back in their empty cot, as in the safe-sleep lesson. If they doze off in a car seat, pram, swing or baby carrier, move them to their empty cot, on their back, as soon as you can.

In the first weeks, it is normal for a baby to doze off during a feed or in your arms, but sleep by itself does not mean they have fed enough. If they doze off before feeding well, or their feeds are few, ask the doctor or nurse how to help them feed, and whether you should wake them to feed. From about four months, try putting them in their cot while drowsy, before they are deeply asleep; this helps them learn to fall asleep in their own cot. It is fine if this does not work every time; there is no set deadline for learning it.

Tell ordinary sleepiness apart from danger signs. Call an ambulance or go to the emergency department immediately if, when you try to wake your baby, they are difficult to wake or do not wake up; if they are unusually floppy, have difficulty breathing, or turn blue or grey; or if their temperature is 38 degrees Celsius or higher and they are under three months old.
try_this: Today: Watch your baby before their next sleep time and notice the first tired signal they give, then help them calm down and put them on their back in their empty cot.
reflection_prompts: What is the first tired signal your baby gives, and how do you usually respond when you notice it?
